lines.text: When you get stitches, a doctor pushes a needle through your skin and pulls it tight to hold the wound shut.
But the thread is only holding things together until your body takes over.
First, the wound swells as your body rushes in to protect it.
Then new cells start weaving collagen across the gap, slowly building fresh skin.
Tiny blood vessels grow through it to feed the new tissue.
And over a few weeks, the skin holds on its own, and the stitches come out.
